goal: `mc language` is the one door through which language data reaches production, the way `mc deploy` is for code: it reads memoro's cutover manifests, runs each act's read, compares the numbers with the manifest, asks Martin before every write, hands the Cloudflare key from the keychain to the child process alone, records every act, and picks up where a run stopped. `mc language promote` is the grammar promotion `mc deploy` no longer does.

Martin sees the language side without asking: `mc language` shows each language's last reading and last run, the `mc` page carries a LANGUAGE section and an interrupted run at the top, and `mc deploy --dry-run` says what is waiting.

This is the memoro-cli half of ruling 31 (`docs/project/mc/rulings.md`); the memoro half is memoro's project `language-manifest` (memoro `docs/project/mc/language-manifest/PLAN.json`), which builds the manifests, the `--json` outputs and the credential helper this verb runs against.
contract: No question, no write. Every act that writes — to production or to the local D1 — runs only after Martin answers `y` or `yes` at a terminal to a question that shows that act's read and its expectations. Without a terminal every subcommand that could write exits 2 before reading anything, as `mc deploy` does (`src/mc/prompt.js` 28-31, `src/mc/commands/deploy.js` 627-632). No flag skips the question, and `MC_NO_PROMPT` refuses rather than assumes.
A deviation stops. An `exact` expectation that does not hold stops the run before the next write and prints that act's `if_not`. `advisory` expectations are printed, never enforced.

The key is never an argument, never printed, never logged, never in Martin's shell. It is read from the keychain and set only in the environment of the child process of an act that names `cloudflare-d1-edit`; `CLOUDFLARE_*` variables already set in mc's own environment are removed from every child, and mc says so once per run.

mc owns the door, memoro owns the content: mc never adds flags to a manifest's commands, never rewrites one, never implements an act. It runs the argument arrays exactly as the manifest gives them, with `cwd` the memoro deploy worktree.

A deploy and a language run never write at the same time: each refuses to start while the other has a live `running` record, decided under the register's lock as `mc deploy` decides one deploy at a time (ruling 30). The repository lease is not used — a deploy does not hold it (`docs/technical/mc-deploy.md` § No lease).
The runner never calls `mc language` and no role tells a session to; it is Martin's verb, like `mc deploy`.
out_of_scope: Anything in memoro — the manifests, the scripts' `--json`, the credential helper, the deploy's grammar check. That is `language-manifest`, which lands first.
A manifest editor, a manifest generator, or validation beyond the fields this plan reads. memoro's `scripts/language-library/lib/cutover-manifest.js` is the manifest's own validator.
Running any act against production in a step session. Every test fakes the child processes; the first real run is Martin's.
The 7403 error's cause (ruling 31) and any retry policy for it.
`mc content` or any data layer other than language.

success_criteria.criterion: A run stops at the first exact deviation and asks nothing before it.
success_criteria.check: Martin runs `mc language run sv-forms-cutover --dry-run` after both projects land: it stops at the first exact check that differs from the 2026-10-09 numbers (act `ingest-saldo` or `purge-wiktionary-forms`), prints the act's `if_not`, asks nothing, and the run record shows no execute.

success_criteria.criterion: The key never leaves the keychain except into the child that needs it.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/commands/language.test.js` asserts the fake spawn's argv never contains the token, only credentialed acts' child env carries `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, the parent's `CLOUDFLARE_*` are stripped, and `mc.log` lines written during the test do not contain the token; `mc language key set` reads the token from stdin.

success_criteria.criterion: Grammar promotion is `mc language promote`, with one question.
success_criteria.check: With nothing waiting, `mc language promote` prints the check's `unchanged` and exits 0 without asking; with rows waiting it shows the count and asks once. Asserted in tests; seen by Martin at the first promotion after `language-manifest` lands.

success_criteria.criterion: The language side is visible without asking.
success_criteria.check: `mc` shows a LANGUAGE section from the cached reading and the last run, and a red line above every section while a run is stopped inside an `opens_gap` window; `mc deploy --dry-run` prints the language line. Asserted in `tests/mc/page.test.js` and `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js`; seen on `mc` in a terminal.

steps.title: The key, the manifests read, and `mc language` / `mc language status <lang>`
steps.done_when: `mc language key set` stores the Cloudflare token (from stdin) and account id in the keychain without either in any argv; `mc language status <lang>` runs the language's reads in the memoro deploy worktree and writes the cache; `mc language` prints every language from the cache; `src/lib/keychain.js` writes secrets through stdin; the tests named here and `mc gate` are green.
instruction: Wait for memoro: this step reads memoro's manifests and `--json` outputs, which `language-manifest` builds. It is blocked on that project; when its four steps are on memoro's `main`, `mc step ready mc-language 1`.

The keychain fix first. `src/lib/keychain.js` `macSet` (lines 69-78) passes the secret as `-w <value>` in `security`'s argv, where `ps` sees it, though the comment says otherwise. Write it through `security -i` instead: spawn `security` with `['-i']` and write one line to its stdin, `add-generic-password -a <account> -s <SERVICE> -w <value> -U\n` with each value double-quoted (verified on this machine 2026-10-10 with an unquoted alphanumeric value: the item is written and read back with `find-generic-password -w`, and nothing of the value is in argv). Refuse a value containing a double quote, a backslash or a newline with a clear error rather than inventing an escaping `security -i` may not honour; a Cloudflare token contains none of them. `run()` (line 208) already accepts `stdinData`. A test in `tests/lib/keychain.test.js` (create it if absent; stub `run`) asserts no argv element contains the value. Every existing caller (`setSecret`) gets the fix for free.

The verb. Add `language: './mc/commands/language.js'` to `VERB_MODULES` (`src/mc-verbs.js` 10-31). The module exports `usage()` (starting `usage`) and `run(argv, deps = {})` taking `stdout`, `stderr`, `env` and every process boundary from `deps`, as `src/mc/commands/prs.js` and `deploy.js` (header lines 48-54) do; parse with `scanArgs` (`src/mc/commands/flags.js` 22). Subcommands in this step: `key set`, `key` (status only), bare `language`, `status <lang>`; the others print 'not yet' and exit 2 until steps 2 and 3. Add the short and full help entries to `src/mc/help-text.js` (THE PAGE list near deploy, lines 36-37; IN FULL near 275-294) — `tests/mc/help.test.js` 56-63 requires `mc language` in the help.

`mc language key set`: reads the token from stdin (refuses with exit 2 when stdin is a TTY and nothing is piped, printing `printf %s "<token>" | mc language key set --account <id>`), takes the account id from `--account <id>` (not secret; it is logged like any identifier), and stores them with `setSecret('cloudflare-d1-edit-token', …)` and `setSecret('cloudflare-account-id', …)`. Precedent: `mc test token --set` (`src/mc/commands/test.js` 434-497) — read it. Never echo either. `mc language key` prints whether both are stored and the account id, never the token. Trap: `src/mc/logger.js` 109-133 logs positional arguments shaped like identifiers; a token passed as an argument would land in `mc.log` — which is why it is stdin only, and why no subcommand takes it positionally.

Where acts run. Every read and write runs with `cwd` the memoro worktree `mc deploy` uses: reuse `deploySource()` and `worktreeState()` (exported from `src/mc/commands/deploy.js`, 289-305 and 313-322). Before a read, `git fetch origin main` and fast-forward that worktree to `origin/main` exactly as `ship()` does (706-713), refusing — touching nothing — when it is dirty or ahead (the rules at 607-625) or when a deploy is running (`runningDeploy`, `src/mc/deploys.js` 144-146). Refuse with a one-line hint when `node_modules/.bin/wrangler` is missing there.

Manifests. Read every `scripts/language-library/cutovers/*.json` from that worktree. Check only what mc uses: `schema === 'memoro-language-cutover'`, `version === 1`, `name`, `lang`, `closes`, `acts[]` with `id`, `title`, `target`, `check`, `execute`, `credentials`, `requires_runnable`, `expect.check`/`expect.execute` (`{path, exact}` | `{path, advisory}`), `if_not`, optional `opens_gap {until, says}`, optional top-level `ran {on, note}`. A manifest with another schema or version is listed as unreadable, by name, and never run. Put this in `src/mc/language-manifest.js` with its own test.

`mc language status <lang>` runs four reads, each `node <script> … --json` in the worktree, each child's stdout parsed as one JSON object: `scripts/language-library/grammar-selector-readiness-report.mjs --env production --langs <lang> --json` (unresolved selectors `languages.<lang>.selectors.unresolved`, rows without a usable selector `languages.<lang>.rows.without_usable_resolved`, and the `uses` of each `unresolved_selectors[]`), `scripts/language-library/readiness-report.mjs --env production --langs <lang> --json` (forms `languages.<lang>.d1.totals.forms`), `scripts/admin/language-grammar-promote.mjs --check --json --langs <lang>` (status and `plans.<lang>.upsert + delete_stale` waiting), and `scripts/language-library/apply-curated-lemma-anchors.mjs --env production --langs <lang> --json` (`would_update`, missing). Reads need no key: give these children the environment without any `CLOUDFLARE_*` (they use wrangler's login). The lemma script exits 1 whenever anchors are missing, even as a read (memoro `apply-curated-lemma-anchors.mjs` lines 30 and 87-89), so a read with a non-zero exit whose stdout still parses is a reading, not a failure. For every `uses` with unresolved selectors, name the manifests whose `closes` contains it. Print one block per language; write the reading to `~/mc/runner/log/language/status-<lang>.json` (`workRoot(env)`, `src/mc/paths.js` 72; `writeFileAtomic`, `src/mc/atomic-write.js` 17) with the time. A read that fails prints its stderr's last lines and the block says so; the others still print.

`mc language` (bare) is offline and instant: one block per language that has a cached reading or a manifest, from the cache files and the run records step 2 writes (absent until then — handle no records), each with the reading's age, and the hint `mc language status <lang>` to refresh. `--json` prints the same as one object.

Tests: `tests/mc/commands/language.test.js` with a temp `MC_WORK_ROOT` (`tests/_isolate-home.mjs` sets one), fake `git`, fake spawn returning canned JSON, fake `getSecret`/`setSecret`; cover key set from stdin and from a TTY, status with a failing read, status naming the closing manifest, bare `language` with no cache, and the refusal when a deploy is running. `tests/mc/language-manifest.test.js` for the reader.

steps.title: `mc language run` and `resume`: preflight, the question, the run record, the deploy exclusion
steps.done_when: `mc language run <manifest> [--dry-run]` and `mc language resume` behave as this step describes, every rule in the plan's contract has a test in `tests/mc/commands/language.test.js` or `tests/mc/language-runs.test.js`, `mc deploy` refuses while a language run is alive (with its test), and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: The run record, `src/mc/language-runs.js`: one JSON file per run at `~/mc/runner/log/language/runs/<started>-<manifest>.json`, written with `writeFileAtomic` on every change: `{ manifest, lang, sha (the worktree's HEAD), started, ended, pid, holder, outcome: running|done|stopped|failed|refused, acts: [{ id, phase: check|execute, outcome: running|passed|deviated|declined|failed|done, started, ended, observed: { <path>: value }, note }] }`. An act's execute row is written `running` before the child starts and its outcome after — as `recordStart`/`recordEnd` do in `src/mc/deploys.js` 171-207. `runAlive(run, {alive})` = outcome `running`, no `ended`, pid alive (`processAlive`, `src/mc/lease-owner.js` 33). `closeAbandoned` marks dead `running` runs `failed` with 'never came back', like `deploys.js` 232-243. Export `liveRun(env)`, `lastRun(env, {manifest?})`, `openGap(env)` (the newest run whose last done execute is an act with `opens_gap` and whose `until` act has no done execute — returns `{ run, act, says }`).

Mutual exclusion, both ways. Under `realLock(root, …)` (`src/mc/register.js` 390), a language run checks `runningDeploy(env, {alive})` and `liveRun(env)`, closes abandoned runs, and writes its record before starting anything. In `src/mc/commands/deploy.js`, `refuseRunning` (592-599) also refuses while `liveRun(env)` is alive: `mc: a language run of <manifest> is running since <when> (pid <pid>) — nothing was deployed`, with a refusal row like the existing one; a test in `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js`.

`run <manifest>`: no terminal → exit 2 before anything (`interactive(env)`, `src/mc/prompt.js` 28-31). Then preflight, all before the first write, any failure stopping with production untouched: (1) the worktree is at `origin/main` (step 1's fast-forward, same refusals); (2) every credential any act names is in the keychain, and a harmless read with it succeeds — run the first credentialed act's `check` with the key in its environment and require exit 0; (3) for every act with `target: 'local'`, its `check` runs and its exact expectations are reported (they decide whether that act's execute is offered or skipped as already true — see below); (4) no deploy and no other run is live; (5) for the first writing act, every id in its `requires_runnable` has its `check` pass with all exact expectations. Print `mc: CLOUDFLARE_* set in this shell are ignored — the key comes from the keychain` when any was set.

Then the acts in order. For each: run its `check`; compare every expectation at its path (missing path = deviation); print `act <n>/<total> <id> — <title>`, each observed value next to its expectation (exact ✓/✗, advisory in dim with its text). An exact deviation stops the run (`stopped`), printing `if_not` and `mc language resume` — except an act whose execute is already recorded `done` in this run, which is skipped. A read-only act (`execute: null`) passes on to the next. A writing act: if every `expect.execute` already holds in the check output, say so and ask whether to run it anyway (default no). Otherwise ask `<id>: write to <target>? [y/N]` with `ask()` (`src/mc/prompt.js` 58-62); anything but `y`/`yes` records `declined`, stops, exit 1. Before every execute of an act with `requires_runnable`, re-run those checks. The execute's stdout is parsed and `expect.execute` compared; deviation or non-zero exit stops the run with `if_not`.

Child processes. Spawn `act.check` / `act.execute` exactly as given (argv array, no shell), `cwd` the worktree, stdout piped (parsed as one JSON object — the last `{…}` block if logs leaked), stderr teed to the terminal and to `~/mc/runner/log/language/<started>-<manifest>.log`. Environment: `scrubRuntimeSecretsFromEnv(process.env)` (`src/mc/runtime-secrets.js` 49) minus `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, plus — only when the act lists `cloudflare-d1-edit` — `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` from `getSecret`. Redact the token from everything written to the terminal and the log, as `src/mc/commands/shot.js` does with `scrubber` (line 271). SIGINT/HUP/TERM forward SIGTERM to the child as `spawnDeployDefault` does (`deploy.js` 122-180); the run is then `stopped` with the act `failed` (interrupted), exit 130.

`--dry-run`: no question, no write. Run every check up to and including the first act whose `execute` targets production, plus that act's `requires_runnable` checks, comparing expectations; list the later acts as `not checkable until <first writing act> has written` with their commands. Exit 0 when all exact expectations hold, 1 at the first deviation. Record it as a run with outcome `done` or `stopped` and `dry_run: true`. A manifest with `ran` prints its `ran.on` and note first.

`resume`: takes the newest run whose outcome is `stopped` or `failed` (or `--manifest <name>`), refuses when its `sha` is not the worktree's HEAD after the fast-forward — the manifest may have changed — unless `--from-head` is given, and starts a new run record linked by `resumes: <started>`. Acts with a `done` execute are skipped. The act whose execute was `running` or `failed` is resumed: its check runs and is shown, its exact check expectations become advisory for this one act (a partial write has changed what it reads), and the question is asked again. Every memoro write the manifests name is idempotent (`INSERT OR REPLACE`, delete-until-empty, upsert — memoro `scripts/language-library/sync-local-to-remote.js` header lines 11-13, `bulk-purge-language-forms.mjs` `runPurge`).

Tests use the temp `MC_WORK_ROOT`, a fixture manifest in `tests/fixtures/language/`, fake spawn, fake `ask`/`interactive`, fake `alive`: no terminal → 2 and nothing spawned; declined → no execute; exact deviation stops before the next write; advisory never stops; `requires_runnable` failing stops the first write; resume skips done acts and relaxes only the interrupted act; the token only in credentialed children; deploy refused while a run lives and a run refused while a deploy lives; dry run stops at the first writing act.

steps.title: `mc language promote`
steps.done_when: `mc language promote [--langs <list>]` checks, shows what waits, asks once, executes with the key, and records the run in the same record as `run`; its tests are green and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: It is a one-act run without a manifest file: build the act in code — `check` `['node', 'scripts/admin/language-grammar-promote.mjs', '--check', '--json', ...(langs ? ['--langs', langs] : [])]`, `execute` the same without `--check`, `credentials: ['cloudflare-d1-edit']`, `target: 'production'` — and hand it to step 2's runner, so the question, the exclusion, the key, the record and resume are the same code. Record it with `manifest: 'grammar-promote'`.

The check's JSON is memoro's `buildPromotionReport` (memoro `scripts/language-library/promote-curated-grammar.mjs` 300-320): for each language `languages.<lang>.status` (`unchanged`, `ready`) and `plans.<lang>.{desired, upsert, delete_stale}`. Nothing `ready` → print `nothing waiting — every language unchanged`, exit 0, no question. Otherwise print one line per ready language — `<lang>: <upsert> to write, <delete_stale> stale to remove, <desired> rows in all` — and ask once: `promote grammar for <langs> to production? [y/N]`. After execute, each language's `status` must be `promoted`; anything else stops with the wrapper's output. A non-zero check exit is the selector or source gate: print the wrapper's lines (memoro's step 4 adds `close it: mc language status <lang>`) and exit 1.

After a successful promote, rewrite the cached status for each promoted language so `mc language` and the page stop showing rows waiting. Tests: nothing waiting, one waiting, declined, gate failure, the token in the execute child only.

steps.title: The page, `mc deploy --dry-run`, and the documents
steps.done_when: The `mc` page has a LANGUAGE section and the open-gap line, `mc deploy --dry-run` prints the language line, the documents and canon lines this step names are updated, the page, deploy and help tests are green, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Page. `src/mc/page-collect.js` `collectPage()` (1225-1404) gains `language`: `{ languages: [{ lang, read_at, unresolved, without_usable, waiting_rows, forms }], last_run, open_gap }` from the cache files and `openGap`/`lastRun` (file reads only — the page is offline and instant). `src/mc/page-render.js` `renderPageLines()` (1280-1349): a `languageLines()` section titled `LANGUAGE`, drawn with `heading(...)` like `deployLines` (398-454) and placed right after DEPLOY; it shows only languages with something to say (unresolved selectors, rows waiting, a reading older than 7 days) plus the last run in one line, and is omitted when there is nothing — the empty page gains no line. When `open_gap` is set, one red line goes above every section: `language: <run manifest> stopped after <act> — <says> · mc language resume`. Tests in `tests/mc/page.test.js`: the section order assertion (1302-1330) gains LANGUAGE after DEPLOY where present; the `--json` fixture keys (1471-1488) gain `language`; the open-gap line; the omitted empty section. If the section title is in the palette table in `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` (title row line 459, checked by page.test.js 2042-2075), add it there.

`mc deploy --dry-run`. Add `deps.languageState` (default: read the cache and `openGap`) to `deployPlan` (`src/mc/commands/deploy.js` 383-433) and a line in `planLines` (453-482) before the closing `--dry-run` line: `mc: language — sv 724 rows waiting (read 2h ago) · mc language promote`, or `mc: language — nothing waiting (read …)`, or `mc: language — no reading; mc language status <lang>`; plus the open-gap line when set. `--json` carries it as `language`. Test in `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js`.

Documents. A new `docs/technical/mc-language.md` modelled on `docs/technical/mc-deploy.md`: the subcommands, the manifest fields mc reads, preflight, the question, the record and resume, the key, the exclusion with deploy, the page. `docs/technical/mc-deploy.md`: the refusal while a language run lives, and that the deploy no longer promotes grammar (memoro's check prints the waiting line). `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`: rows for `mc language` and its subcommands under the current model (lines 26-66), in a final commit touching nothing else (`docs/coding-agent-protocol.md` 126-129). `canon/roles/_session-work.md` line 13: `mc deploy`, `mc language`, production data… — so no session drives it. A `changelog.d/mc-language.md` fragment (`section: Added`) per `changelog.d/README.md`.
